note: Seljuks capture Baghdad (1055) and become protectors of the Abbasid Caliph; the caliph retains religious legitimacy while Seljuk sultans hold all real power.

_quarry.structural_significance: The Seljuk sultanate's protection of the Abbasid caliph while stripping him of political power pioneered the sultan/caliph dual sovereignty model adopted by the Mamluks and later Ottomans; this arrangement allowed Islamic imperial governance to continue even when the caliphal family held only ceremonial authority.
